sections.title: Clean accepted hard surfaces without damaging decoration
sections.text: The provider uses compatible physical cleaning on accepted stable surfaces, supporting fragile pieces and collecting deposits from accessible attachment points. A painted coating that transfers during the trial changes the recovery plan; it is not scrubbed until the mark disappears. Absorbent ribbons, glued paper and inaccessible interiors receive separate replacement or specialist decisions.

sections.title: Dry and pack with clean separators
sections.text: Accepted items are inspected and dried before packing in clean protective material. An ornament is not returned to an affected cardboard divider merely because its exterior has been cleaned. The receiving storage area must have its moisture problem and any applicable remediation review addressed before the recovered collection returns.

sections.title: Provider and independent evaluation
sections.text: Go Green’s own Texas Mold Remediation Contractor license remains pending. Before license-required work begins, we will verify the partner’s applicable contractor and company credentials, identify the performing provider and confirm its scope. Independent assessment and any required clearance are separate services.

mold-contaminated-contents-cleaning/mine.estimate: Finish stability, fragile construction, attached porous parts and collection value shape recovery. Share an inventory and representative photographs.
checklist: Separate fragile or valuable ornaments in the inventory.
Identify tissue, cardboard and fabric attachments.
Describe painted finishes and prior cleaning.

fire-damaged-debris-removal/mineral-well.intro: Fire damaged debris removal in Mineral Wells may be needed after a small garage fire leaves melted plastic shelving and charred stored lumber against a shared wall. We will remove the approved debris, separate sharp or unstable pieces, and keep the carry route clear of loose ash.

sections.title: Fire damaged debris removal in Mineral Wells: Mark debris boundaries and protect the route
sections.text: The site release and debris list are confirmed before removal. Nearby tools and contents are moved or covered, and the path from garage to disposal container is protected. Heat-damaged wall material is identified for a separate assessment rather than mixed with loose contents.

sections.title: Break down unstable shelving and lumber
sections.text: Melted shelving can bind stored objects together or leave a brittle leg carrying an unstable stack. We support and unload accessible approved items before the shelf is cut or released, containing sharp plastic fragments at the work area. Charred loose lumber is separated from building framing and carried in manageable stable loads; pulling the whole fused pile from the wall is not the removal method.

sections.title: Collect ash and inspect the shared-wall edge
sections.text: Loose ash and fragments are collected from the floor and lower wall after bulky items leave. The exposed wall and remaining stored goods are checked for heat damage and soot. Cleanup of retained building surfaces follows a separate included scope.

fire-damaged-debris-removal/mineral-well.estimate: Debris quantity, sharp materials, garage access, and disposal requirements affect the estimate. Share a safe overview and the approved removal boundary.
checklist: Identify debris approved for removal.
Describe melted, sharp, or unstable materials.
Note the carry route and shared-wall concerns.

fire-damaged-contents-cleaning/mineral-w.intro: Fire damaged contents cleaning in Mineral Wells may be useful when a garage fire leaves soot on hard tool cases and a painted metal workbench while paper labels and foam inserts remain inside. We will separate cleanable hard surfaces from porous components and document items requiring replacement or specialist review.

sections.title: Fire damaged contents cleaning in Mineral Wells: Inventory contents before moving them
sections.text: Each case is recorded with its lid, latch, handle, and interior insert assessed separately. Items are moved onto protected staging so soot does not transfer to clean surfaces. Electronics, adhesives, and safety equipment are held for specialist or manufacturer review.

sections.title: Clean accepted cases and bench surfaces
sections.text: Accepted cases are opened so soot beneath removable foam can be evaluated separately from the outer shell. Suitable plastic or metal surfaces receive compatible cleaning at hinges, latches and the exposed base, while smoke-affected foam that cannot be adequately restored receives a replacement decision. Tool labels needed for identification are preserved where possible or documented before approved removal; powered tools remain in their separate service pathway.

sections.title: Repack only after inspection
sections.text: Cleaned cases are allowed to dry and checked at their seams before accepted tools return. The inventory notes items cleaned, replaced, or referred, avoiding a blanket recovery claim for mixed contents. Building soot and odor remain a separate property-cleaning scope.

fire-damaged-contents-cleaning/mineral-w.estimate: Contents value, electronics, foam inserts, and soot depth determine which items can be handled. Share an inventory and photographs of the cases.
checklist: Identify hard cases and sensitive contents.
Describe soot on seams, handles, or interiors.
List tools requiring electronics or safety review.

fire-extinguisher-residue-cleanup/minera.intro: Fire extinguisher residue cleanup in Mineral Wells can involve powder in the joints and underside ribs of interlocking garage floor tiles. We will identify the agent and lift approved tiles so cleaning reaches deposits that a pass over the top surface misses.

sections.title: Fire extinguisher residue cleanup in Mineral Wells: inspect the removable floor
sections.text: The agent information and tile product guide collection and cleaning. We identify whether the tiles are designed to release, protect the remaining floor and collect loose surface deposits before movement. Brittle heat-damaged pieces and any affected powered equipment receive separate decisions.

sections.title: Clean the interlocks and underside as tiles are lifted
sections.text: Approved tiles are supported and released without shaking powder across cleared areas. Suitable filtered collection removes loose identified dry agent, followed by compatible cleaning of accessible ribs, locking edges and the exposed slab. Trapped powder in a damaged closed recess may make replacement preferable to forcing cleaning liquid through the joint.

sections.title: Reset accepted tiles on a cleaned dry base
sections.text: The slab and accepted tile parts are inspected after the selected treatment and dried before reassembly. Remaining deposits beneath adjacent rows require additional access rather than a declaration that the visible field is finished. Damaged locks and heat deformation have their own replacement decision, separate from residue removal.

fire-extinguisher-residue-cleanup/minera.estimate: Agent, tile release method, underside geometry and residue spread affect work. Share the extinguisher label and flooring product.
checklist: Identify removable interlocking floor tiles.
Describe powder beneath edges or joints.
Share agent information and previous cleanup.

emergency-board-up-after-fire/mineral-we.intro: Emergency board up after fire in Mineral Wells may be needed when a garage side door is damaged and the frame no longer holds its latch, leaving tools and equipment exposed. We will measure the opening, identify sound fastening points, and install a temporary closure that keeps the approved access route usable.

sections.title: Emergency board up after fire in Mineral Wells: Check the damaged frame and safe entry
sections.text: The site is released and loose glass or splintered material is controlled before measurement. The installer checks whether the jamb and adjacent framing can take fasteners without loading a burned or loosened section. Access needs for occupants and emergency responders are recorded.

sections.title: Fit the temporary panel to sound attachment points
sections.text: If the damaged door cannot latch, we establish whether the opening can be closed entirely or must serve an approved entry route. A fixed panel is fastened to sound receiving members only where closing the doorway is permitted; an access requirement needs a suitable temporary entry arrangement. The burned jamb is not made into a reliable fastening point by adding more screws.

sections.title: Inspect coverage and route clearance
sections.text: Fasteners, perimeter coverage, and panel stability are checked after installation. The work record notes whether the original door can still be used or must remain closed. Permanent door and frame replacement are separate repairs.

emergency-board-up-after-fire/mineral-we.estimate: Opening dimensions, frame damage, exterior exposure, and access needs determine the board-up setup. Share safe photos and any entry restrictions.
checklist: Identify the damaged door or opening.
Describe frame condition and access needs.
Share site release or safety instructions.

crawl-space-sewage-cleanup/mineral-wells.intro: Crawl space sewage cleanup in Mineral Wells can include contaminated insulation held by mesh beneath the floor. We will remove the specified wet insulation and evaluate its supporting material separately so a dirty restraint is not left against clean replacement batts.

sections.title: Crawl space sewage cleanup in Mineral Wells: identify the insulation restraint
sections.text: After the source and safe entry conditions are addressed, we distinguish wire supports from woven mesh, facing and utility hangers. The supported insulation and any retained liquid are accounted for before a restraint is released. Mesh that also conceals services is not cut blindly to speed removal.

sections.title: Contain insulation and decide what support can remain
sections.text: Specified contaminated batts and unsuitable absorbent or damaged mesh are lowered into controlled waste collection. Suitable accessible hard restraints may receive physical cleaning followed by appropriate disinfection, while material holding waste in inaccessible fibers or overlaps requires removal. Staples and wire ends released with the mesh are collected so they do not remain in the work or crawl route.

sections.title: Clean exposed wood before new supports are attached
sections.text: The newly exposed joist and subfloor faces are checked for waste deposits, physically cleaned as included and evaluated for drying. The installer replaces failed restraints after the underlying surfaces have been addressed, using the appropriate attachment for the insulation system. Ground contamination and the plumbing repair retain their own scopes rather than being counted as complete with the insulation removal.

crawl-space-sewage-cleanup/mineral-wells.estimate: Restraint material, attachment, insulation saturation and crawl clearance affect handling. Share existing inspection photographs and plumbing findings.
checklist: Identify mesh, wire or facing below the insulation.
Describe hanging material without entering the crawl area.
Share source repair and utility restrictions.
